name: Ketengban
catalog_citation: Sims, Andrew & Anne Sims (1982). Ketengban Phonology. Workpapers in Indonesian Linguistics [= Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures] 1: 50-74. Ambon: Summer Institute of Linguistics.
catalog_locator: pp. 50-52 (sections 1, 1.1 Stress, 1.2 Shape of the Phonological Word); p. 72 (complex nuclei, criteria 1-2)
catalog_quote: The phonological word (PW) in Ketengban is the domain of one stress. The stressed syllable is frequently, but not always, accompanied by higher pitch than the non-stressed syllables. The majority of PWs consist of one to three syllables although words of up to five syllables are known to occur. 1.1 Stress. Stress is phonemic, as evidenced by the following contrasts: Between nouns: /'bume/ ['bumɛ] 'horsefly' /bu'me/ [bu'mɛ] 'short' /'kalum/ ['kalum] 'charcoal' /ka'lum/ [ka'lum] 'tapioca type' Between noun and verb: /'bana/ ['bana] 'to walk' /ba'na/ [ba'na] 'jaw' /'galuna/ ['galuna] 'vegetable type' /ga'luna/ [ga'luna] 'to wear net bag with base on head' ... Between verbs: /'kouna/ ... 'to bundle up' /kou'na/ ... 'to plant' ... 1.2 Shape of the Phonological Word. PWs exhibit the following syllable and stress patterns: One-syllable words: 'S ...
